title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (section 8): Grothendieck wants a heuristic count of the Frobenius eigenvalues on the 'vanishing' crystalline cohomology of a hyperplane section that are p-adic units. In modern terms, this is the slope-0 (unit-root) part.

Setting: X is smooth, proper, connected of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p, with X ⊂ P^r. Y is a hyperplane section and W = W(k). He posits a crystalline cohomology H(X), a complex over W with H(X) ⊗^L_W k = H_DR(X). This gives the universal coefficient sequences 0 → H^i ⊗ k → H^i_DR → Tor_1^W(H^{i+1}, k) → 0 for X and for Y. The restriction maps u = (u_0, u_1, u_2) between them yield, by the snake lemma, the exact sequence (8.1.3) with E(Y) = Coker(H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y)). The relevant map is u_2 : H^n(X)[p] → H^n(Y)[p].

This page, part 8.2 (struck through with diagonal pencil lines, but its content is used later), dualises u_2 by assuming integral Poincaré duality including torsion. For a smooth proper Z of dimension d, Tors H^i is dual to Tors H^{2d+1-i}, and for a finite-length W-module T, T[p] is dual to T^D ⊗ k. Hence:
- H^n(Y)[p] is dual to Tors^{n-1}(Y) ⊗ k (Y has dimension n-1).
- H^n(X)[p] is dual to Tors^{n+1}(X) ⊗ k.
- u_2 is the transpose of u'_2 : Tors^{n-1}(Y) ⊗ k → Tors^{n+1}(X) ⊗ k, induced by the Gysin map H^{n-1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X).
- So Ker u_2 is dual to Coker u'_2, and Coker u_2 is dual to Ker u'_2.

Part 8.3: by analogy with ℓ-adic cohomology, use weak Lefschetz with Z/ℓ^n coefficients. U = X − Y is affine, so H^{n-1}_c(U, Z/ℓ) = 0. Hence H^n_c(U, Z_ℓ) is torsion-free, and E(Y), which injects into it, is torsion-free. Also H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y) is injective. Together these give Tors^{n-1}(X) ≅ Tors^{n-1}(Y). He postulates the same in crystalline cohomology.

Since Gysin ∘ restriction is cup product with the hyperplane class, u'_2 becomes the Lefschetz operator L : Tors^{n-1}(X) ⊗ k → Tors^{n+1}(X) ⊗ k. This is independent of Y, so the last term Coker u_2 of (8.1.3) (dual to Ker L) is independent of Y. In addition, E(Y) being torsion-free means rank E(Y) = dim_k E(Y) ⊗ k, and Frobenius eigenvalues on E(Y) ⊗ k are the mod-p reductions of those on E(Y).

On the next page the plan is completed:
- Ker u_0 = 0.
- Pass to F-semisimple parts (an exact functor, equivalent to F_p-étale data).
- This compares the number of unit-root eigenvalues on E(Y) with the semisimple part of the de Rham / Hodge vanishing cohomology, up to error terms bounded independently of Y.
errors: 'l'homomorphisme u est transposé' should read u_2 (only the third component is meant).

The integral crystalline facts used are explicitly assumed, not proved. These are: Poincaré duality including the torsion linking pairing, and integral weak Lefschetz (injectivity on H^{n-1} with torsion-free cokernel). The previous page's margin even notes Poincaré duality is unfortunately not available. Whether the torsion-free-cokernel statement holds crystallinely in general is not something I can confirm.
Minor: the transcription treats the 8.2 passage as deleted. It is crossed by diagonal lines, but the next paragraph relies on (8.2.1), so it is a superseded draft rather than abandoned content.
Dating: the reference to Berthelot on the previous page places the text around 1970 or later, not 1958.

ideas.what: Dualising the torsion term Tor_1(H^n, k) via integral Poincaré duality: H^i[p] dual to Tors^{2d+1-i} ⊗ k, and restriction transposed to Gysin.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion linking pairing / integral crystalline duality (Berthelot; Ekedahl's duality for de Rham–Witt)

ideas.what: Weak Lefschetz with torsion coefficients implies the vanishing-cycle cokernel E(Y) is torsion-free and Tors^{n-1}(X) ≅ Tors^{n-1}(Y); postulated for crystalline cohomology.
ideas.modern_name: Integral weak Lefschetz theorem (crystalline version by Berthelot)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; SGA 4 / SGA 7 for étale; Berthelot (CRAS 1973) for crystalline
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XIV (affine Lefschetz), SGA 7 (vanishing cycles), étale case

ideas.what: Identification of Gysin∘restriction with the Lefschetz operator on torsion, making the error term in the hyperplane-section snake sequence independent of Y.
ideas.modern_name: Hard-Lefschetz-type operator on torsion of crystalline cohomology

ideas.what: Overall programme: estimate the number of unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues of vanishing crystalline cohomology of hyperplane sections via F-semisimple parts of de Rham / Hodge cohomology, with Y-independent error terms.
ideas.modern_name: Unit-root (slope 0) part / p-rank of hyperplane sections; generic ordinarity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bloch–Kato–Illusie (slope spectral sequence), Illusie 'Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales' (1990)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a heuristic comparing the unit-root count of the vanishing crystalline cohomology E(Y) with the semisimple part of E_DR(Y), with error terms controlled by the torsion of H^*(X) via the Lefschetz operator and independent of Y. This anticipates questions on p-ranks and ordinarity of (generic) hyperplane sections, later treated by Illusie and others, but this specific torsion-bookkeeping approach does not seem recorded.
missed.quote: La chose importante pour nous est que ce morphisme (donc son Ker) ne dépend plus du choix de Y, donc ... le dernier terme de (8.1.3) ... ne dépend plus de Y.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a uniform-in-Y bound on the defect between the p-rank (étale F_p data) and the slope-0 multiplicity for vanishing cohomology of hyperplane sections. This is relevant to generic ordinarity questions, though modern techniques (Illusie, de Rham–Witt) likely subsume it.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual steps (torsion duality, integral weak Lefschetz, Gysin∘restriction = Lefschetz operator) are standard. The interest lies in the unpublished heuristic programme of section 8 on unit-root eigenvalues of vanishing cohomology, which foreshadows ordinarity questions, but this page itself is routine bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: The top block (through 'Ker u'_2') is crossed out by diagonal pencil strokes rather than marked as a normal deletion. Only the inserted 'dual de' replaces 'isomorphe à'.

The handwritten insertion above 'situation analogue' reads 'en cohomologie ℓ-adique (ℓ ≠ p)'. Above 'de Lefschetz' it reads 'faible (pour les coefficients Z/ℓ^n Z)', and 'théorème' replaces 'les assertions'.
The subscript of u in 'u_0 : H^{n-1}(X) → H^{n-1}(Y)' is overwritten in the typescript; 0 is the intended reading.
The marginal note near 'donc aussi du' is a struck-out handwritten fragment, illegible. 'le' is added before 'dernier terme'.
